messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Colorimetric enzyme test strip reaction for measuring glucose concentration in a fluid sample, run as a series of small droplet reactions on a lab-on-a-chip device.

REAGENTS USED:
  - glucose sample: the fluid being tested; five separate portions are used, one per trial, so a small calibration-style series of readings can be built up
  - enzyme reagent: a ready-mixed reagent containing glucose oxidase and peroxidase along with a color-forming dye; it reacts with glucose to produce a colored product, with more color developing as more glucose is present
  - distilled water: used in a side reaction alongside the reagent, prepared and set aside for each trial but not measured

STEPS:
1. Place a small portion of the glucose sample on the chip.
2. Add a small portion of the enzyme reagent next to it.
3. Bring the two together and mix them for about 10 seconds so the reaction can begin.
4. Hold the combined droplet in place and measure the color/light signal it gives off for 30 seconds. This reading reflects how much glucose was in the sample.
5. Separately, combine a portion of distilled water with a portion of the enzyme reagent, mix for 30 seconds, and discard it.
6. Repeat steps 1-5 four more times, for a total of five trials. In each trial the amount of glucose sample stays the same, but the amount of enzyme reagent added is changed (first a small amount, then twice as much, then twice as much again, then twice as much again, before returning to the original small amount for the fifth trial).
7. After all five trials are complete, discard the reacted droplets from each trial.

INTERPRETATION: Each of the five trials produces a signal reading whose strength corresponds to how much glucose was present in that sample. Comparing the five readings against each other (or against known glucose standards run the same way) lets a technician build a calibration curve and estimate the glucose concentration of an unknown sample. A stronger signal generally means more glucose reacted with the reagent.

module absorbance

manifest reagent
manifest glucose
manifest distilled_water
manifest Sample

instructions:

aa = dispense 10 units of glucose
bb = dispense 10 units of reagent
result1 = mix aa with bb for 10s
reading1 = detect absorbance on result1 for 30s
aaa = dispense 10 units of distilled_water
bbb = dispense 10 units of reagent
a = mix aaa with bbb for 30s
dispose a

cc = dispense 10 units of glucose
dd = dispense 20 units of reagent
result2 = mix cc with dd for 10s
reading2 = detect absorbance on result2 for 30s
ccc = dispense 10 units of distilled_water
ddd = dispense 10 units of reagent
a = mix ccc with ddd for 30s
dispose a

ee = dispense 10 units of glucose
ff = dispense 40 units of reagent
result3 = mix ee with ff for 10s
reading3 = detect absorbance on result3 for 30s
eee = dispense 10 units of distilled_water
fff = dispense 10 units of reagent
a = mix eee with fff for 30s
dispose a

gg = dispense 10 units of glucose
hh = dispense 80 units of reagent
result4 = mix gg with hh for 10s
reading4 = detect absorbance on result4 for 30s
ggg = dispense 10 units of distilled_water
hhh = dispense 10 units of reagent
a = mix ggg with hhh for 30s
dispose a

ii = dispense 10 units of glucose
jj = dispense 10 units of reagent
result5 = mix ii with jj for 10s
reading5 = detect absorbance on result5 for 30s
iii = dispense 10 units of distilled_water
jjj = dispense 10 units of reagent
a = mix iii with jjj for 30s

dispose a
dispose result1
dispose result2
dispose result3
dispose result4
dispose result5

metadata.protocol_name: Colorimetric Enzyme Test Strip Reaction (Srinivasan et al. 2004)

sources.title: Droplet-based microfluidic lab-on-a-chip for clinical diagnostics on standard environmental fluids

metadata.notes: The .bs code matches the colorimetric enzyme-kinetic method (Trinder's reaction) described in Srinivasan et al. 2004. The 30s detect time aligns exactly, and the 10s mix time closely approximates the 15s in the source. Notable differences introduced by the benchmark author include varying the reagent volume rather than the glucose concentration to construct the calibration curve, and the inclusion of an unread water+reagent blank step which the source explicitly states is not required. The detection method was updated from 'fluorescence' to 'absorbance' to accurately reflect the colorimetric nature of the cited assay.

operation_evidence.source_quote: color signal is read continuously for at least 30 seconds

numeric_mismatches.source_value: does not require a blank reading
